C3.rationale: Level 1 fits: digital and AI content is present but confined to stream-specific optional courses rather than a documented core, and the bulk of it is tool operation and training (Python programming in SCIE1000, GIS software, database SQL). The level-2 anchor requires CORE units to address AI capabilities AND limitations/ethics with use-with-limits assessed; the extract documents no compulsory unit, and the two AI-bearing courses sit inside particular pathways (STAT3007 Deep Learning within statistics; BIOL1000 within biology). BIOL1000 names ethical AI use in one outcome and carries an assessment titled for the AI era, but neither documents AI capabilities and limitations as the assessed object, so it does not carry level 2 on its own. Far from level 3, which requires assessed critique or governance of AI systems (bias, accountability, transparency, regulation, data governance) in the discipline's own context.

G1.rationale: The FAIL condition - generic or interchangeable content without disciplinary identity - is what the extract documents at program grain. The program describes itself as a versatile degree balancing a defined sequence against flexible course options, and its structure section lists 57 prescribed units spanning unrelated disciplines (archaeology, philosophy, psychology, mathematics, chemistry, geology, public health) with no unit documented as compulsory for every student. No all-compulsory specialist core, no accredited sequence and no program-level staged prerequisite chain appears; prerequisite statements exist only inside individual course descriptions. The specialist depth would sit in the extended majors and majors named on the program page, but the extract carries none of their structures, so a PASS cannot be evidenced from this capture.

ambiguities: Whole-panel: the extract documents no compulsory course. The structure section calls all 57 units 'prescribed for this academic program', but the program text also describes 'flexible course options' and 48 units of study, so no unit is provably taken by every student. Resolved by the lower-level rule at two grains: assessment evidence in prescribed units is accepted for level 2 where the feature recurs across many pathways (C1 collaboration, C4 transfer, C5 inquiry, W1 communication, W2 task fidelity), but every level-3 anchor requiring a feature to recur across the program, to be required, or to be the assessment spine is refused for the same reason.

C3 straddled levels 1 and 2. BIOL1000 names the ethical use of AI in an outcome and carries an assessment sequence titled 'Inquiry and Synthesis in the AI Era', and STAT3007 assesses whether a deep learning algorithm is appropriate for an application - both read toward level 2. Neither is a documented core unit, and neither documents AI capabilities and limitations as the assessed object, so the lower level (AI appearing only in elective/stream courses and as tool operation) was taken.

C4 straddled levels 2 and 3. SCIE3122 is a self-scoped supervised research project assessed by proposal, seminar and report, which reads as the level-3 exemplar, but it is entered by supervisor approval and permission to enrol, so it is a route rather than documented progression; the lower level was taken.

C5 straddled levels 2 and 3. SCIE3122 and SCIE3221 assess a supervised project with a hurdle seminar presentation, which approaches defence under scrutiny, but the level-3 anchor requires the project to be REQUIRED and not one route among several; the lower level was taken.

W1 straddled levels 2 and 3. AGRC3042 carries an 'Industry Expert Panel Discussion - Participation' task and SCIE3010 delivers to a community audience, which point at level 3's external practitioner audience, but participation is pass/fail, no assessed criteria name professional conduct or accountability, and no progressive sequence of communication assessment is documented; the lower level was taken.

One-construct-one-home: SCIE3050's placement evidence was scored only in W3, never in C1 or C4; AGRC3042's stakeholder-communication task was scored in C1 as assessed collaborative/stakeholder practice rather than in W1, and W1 rests on separate evidence (The Conversation article, SCIE3010 community delivery).
notScoreable: G1: the extract omits the structure of every extended major, major and minor named on the program page. A coherent specialist core with progressive depth, if it exists, would be documented there. The gate has no third state, so it is recorded as FAIL on the evidence captured, but a recapture that includes at least one major's structure could change the result.

C3 governance route: no evidence about AI bias, accountability, transparency, regulation or data governance appears anywhere in the extract, so the level-3 anchor could not be tested rather than merely failing.

Two prescribed units carry no learning outcomes and only an aggregate assessment line in the extract (BIOL3016 'Final exam, essay, field report: 100%'; GEOS3004; UQLD3000; SCIE3040), and three of those are marked as not currently offered, so they contributed no item evidence.
